response.markdown_report:
At 0% progress, the strongest next step is a **paired temporal-sensitivity audit for the existing HSTU**, establishing measured failure modes before changing training.

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Current margins measure training-pair separation. They cannot establish validation ranking quality. (2) Left padding makes final-position extraction critical. The adapter should explicitly verify the last nonpadding index. (3) Feedback distinguishes specific recent interests from broad associations. Histories alone cannot establish fulfilled needs or compatibility.

**Related-work insights.** (1) HSTU models nonstationary streams [1]. Its architecture does not prove that this checkpoint uses ordering effectively. (2) Controlled-shuffling studies motivate separating final-event dependence from broader sequence sensitivity [2]. Perturbation effects remain descriptive, potentially reflecting distribution shift. (3) TREC distinguishes complementarity from unknown compatibility [3]. Missing specifications must therefore remain unknown. (4) Sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons [4]. The pinned benchmark must remain the sole selection criterion.

**Framework and directions.**

| Direction | Existing evidence | Missing measurement |
|---|---|---|
| Temporal dependence | Training margins | Paired sensitivity to recent versus older events |
| Evidence sufficiency | Titles/descriptions | Supported, conflicting, or unknown attributes |
| Ranking robustness | Pinned validation HR@10 | Candidate-dependent disagreement |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means more work.

1. **Paired temporal audit [1,2]: 4/8/3.** Originality: + integrates controls into the family adapter; − perturbation probes are established. Potential: + identifies actionable dependence; − sensitivity cannot establish preference. Difficulty: + requires inference only; − careful repacking and pairing are essential.
2. **Evidence-status audit [3]: 5/7/6.** Originality: + separates unknown information from conflict; − attribute audits already exist. Potential: + exposes unsupported compatibility claims; − sparse descriptions limit coverage. Difficulty: + explicit spans are inspectable; − accurate extraction needs annotated validation.
3. **Candidate stress audit [4]: 3/7/5.** Originality: + connects ranking failures to candidate composition; − sampling sensitivity is established. Potential: + reveals fragile improvements; − alternate candidates cannot replace benchmark selection. Difficulty: + reuses scoring; − eligibility and false-negative controls require care.

**Selected algorithm.** Cache up to ten training-loader batches. For each valid sequence, compare equal-count deletion of recent, older, and randomly selected events, retaining at least one event. Also shuffle earlier events while preserving the final event. Left-pad each result and score the original final-position positive/negative pair through ModelView.

Report paired margin changes, pairwise-order flips, feature cosine changes, eligible counts, and uncertainty intervals clustered by user when user identities are available. Otherwise report descriptive summaries without user-level intervals. Return null for unavailable measurements. These are training diagnostics, not HR@10 estimates or causal findings.

Preserve both diagnostic entry points, restore model mode, and retain one checkpoint per category. Any later training intervention requires the unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10 and consistent predictor serialization.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152; [2] https://publications.hse.ru/en/chapters/984043670; [3] https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html; [4] https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/

idea.description: Add a paired temporal-sensitivity diagnostic to the supplied HSTU ModelView adapter. Compare original histories with controlled deletions and shuffling while holding the scored positive/negative pair fixed.
idea.motivation: The current diagnostics measure embedding geometry and sampled training margins but do not reveal whether HSTU responds to recent activity, older context, or ordering beyond the final item. The qualitative feedback motivates measuring these distinctions without assuming that observed purchases establish ownership, satisfied needs, or compatibility.
idea.implementation_notes: Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Use view.model.eval() under torch.no_grad(), restoring the original mode afterward. Cache at most ten batches and use a local seed-42 generator. For each sequence, locate its final nonpadding index using masked position indices, never count-1. Score the positive and negative targets at that original index against every perturbed representation. Remove equal numbers of valid events for recent, older, and random deletion, retaining at least one event; report eligibility by intervention. Repack retained events with left padding. Shuffle only earlier valid events for the final-preserving shuffle. Use predict_score with features shaped B x 1 x D and candidates B x 1 x 2 if required by the existing compatibility contract. Return metrics and explicit metric_definitions, including missing-value reasons. Loader batches have no user identifiers, so do not assume rows are independent users or produce user-level bootstrap intervals unless identities are separately available. Keep existing measured diagnostics but replace fabricated zero defaults with null and counts. No training, architecture, checkpoint, predictor, dataset-routing, or evaluator changes are required by this proposal. Any implementation must retain DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and the supplied training limits and seeds.
idea.pseudocode:
was_training = view.model.training
view.model.eval()
try:
  with no_grad():
    for _, seq, pos, neg in first_ten_cached_batches:
      end = last_nonpadding_index(seq)
      eligible = valid_end_and_nonzero_targets(seq, pos, neg, end)
      candidates = stack(pos[row, end], neg[row, end])
      original = final_nonpadding_feature(view.log2feats(seq), seq)
      original_scores = view.predict_score(original[:, None, :], candidates[:, None, :])
      for intervention in [delete_recent, delete_older, delete_random, shuffle_preserving_final]:
        altered, intervention_eligible = intervene_and_left_pad(seq, local_seed_42)
        features = final_nonpadding_feature(view.log2feats(altered), altered)
        scores = view.predict_score(features[:, None, :], candidates[:, None, :])
        record_paired_margin_changes_order_flips_and_feature_cosines(
          original_scores, scores, original, features,
          eligible & intervention_eligible)
  return {'metrics': summarize_with_counts_and_missing_reasons(),
          'metric_definitions': explicit_definitions_and_limitations()}
finally:
  view.model.train(was_training)

# diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) embeds measured metrics and
# definitions, requesting evidence-grounded interpretations and separating
# observed sensitivity from unverified explanations.

originality.positive: Combines temporal controls, explicit missingness, and HSTU-compatible scoring in the existing diagnostic interface.
originality.negative: Deletion and shuffling probes are established techniques; the contribution is a careful adaptation.

future_potential.positive: Provides a practical basis for deciding whether subsequent single-model changes should address recent-event dependence or broader context use.
future_potential.negative: Training-pair sensitivity may not predict validation gains and cannot establish user intent.

code_difficulty.positive: Uses existing inference hooks and requires no additional trained model or external data.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct masking, paired targets, intervention eligibility, and dependence-aware uncertainty require care.

related_work.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU for recommendation streams and motivates preserving the supplied backbone family.
limitations: Published architecture results do not establish temporal sensitivity of this checkpoint.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential?
contributions: Provides precedent for controlled shuffling to examine sequential structure.
limitations: Shuffling can induce distribution shift; observed effects do not identify causal preferences.

related_work.title: TREC 2025 Recommendation Task
contributions: Distinguishes complementary relevance from established compatibility, including unknown compatibility.
limitations: Its judgment framework does not supply compatibility labels for these Amazon histories.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled evaluation can change model comparisons.
limitations: Does not calibrate this benchmark's sampled HR@10 to full-catalog performance.
